styles.name: Bauhaus
styles.description: A mascot constructed from disciplined primary geometric shapes, clear spatial hierarchy, and flat graphic color.

instructions.materials: Use opaque matte graphic fills with clean geometric boundaries and no simulated natural material.
instructions.forms: Build compact anatomy from circles, rectangles, triangles, and arcs, assigning a clear role to each shape.
instructions.linework: Use minimal uniform linework only where shape boundaries cannot distinguish facial or limb details.
instructions.shading: Keep surfaces flat and define overlaps through clear shape occlusion rather than gradients or drop shadows.
instructions.palette: Choose a small disciplined palette with strong value contrast, allowing approved identity colors to replace conventional primaries.
instructions.texture: Keep color fields smooth and untextured, with no distress, grain, or decorative pattern.
instructions.rendering: Render a readable geometric character whose shape system stays consistent across every required animation pose.

negative_constraints: Do not add poster typography, diagrams, background grids, or unrelated floating geometry.
Avoid mechanically perfect symmetry when the approved character requires asymmetric features.
No scenery, floor shadows, detached decorations, clipped extremities, or changing surface motifs between animation frames.
use_cases: Clear geometric mascots, pictograms, and simplified character systems.
limitations: Geometric reduction must retain enough facial and anatomical landmarks to preserve character identity.

compatibility.scaling: Keep the fixed target cell geometry; downsample the isolated artwork once with the recommended filter, preserve alpha, and inspect facial details at actual size.
notes: Use antialiased geometric borders with opaque fills; keep narrow inter-shape gaps visible at actual size.
Keep texture landmarks and material highlights anchored to the approved character across all poses.

styles.name: Memphis Design
styles.description: A playful graphic mascot combining blocky geometry, bold pattern panels, and deliberate visual asymmetry.

instructions.materials: Use opaque flat graphic color with large patterned surface panels and crisp printed-looking edges.
instructions.forms: Construct a compact character from rounded blocks, wedges, and playful asymmetrical shape combinations.
instructions.linework: Use bold contour strokes and a few oversized squiggle or zigzag markings contained within the body.
instructions.shading: Keep shading flat or use a single offset interior color plane without a detached drop shadow.
instructions.palette: Choose a coordinated high-contrast palette with limited accent colors and a clearly separated facial region.
instructions.texture: Assign one or two broad dot, stripe, or squiggle patterns to fixed body regions with stable registration.
instructions.rendering: Render the patterned mascot alone with attached limbs and no confetti, surrounding shapes, or poster composition.

negative_constraints: Do not surround the character with unrelated floating patterns or geometric decorations.
Avoid tiny all-over patterns, unreadable patterned faces, and random motif placement between frames.
No scenery, floor shadows, detached decorations, clipped extremities, or changing surface motifs between animation frames.
use_cases: Playful patterned mascots and expressive geometric character branding.
limitations: Patterns need large stable motifs; complex all-over decoration can overpower expression at cell size.

compatibility.scaling: Keep the fixed target cell geometry; downsample the isolated artwork once with the recommended filter, preserve alpha, and inspect facial details at actual size.
notes: Preserve antialiased outlines and opaque pattern fills; verify key colors against every pattern accent.

styles.name: Geometric Minimalism
styles.description: A sparse mascot distilled into a few purposeful geometric masses and maximally legible facial marks.

instructions.materials: Use flat opaque digital shapes with uniform untextured surfaces and no simulated material effects.
instructions.forms: Reduce the character to a small number of circles, capsules, and wedges that retain signature anatomy.
instructions.linework: Use either no outline or one consistent thin-but-readable contour; keep the face to a few deliberate marks.
instructions.shading: Avoid modeling except for one clearly defined overlap value where needed for pose readability.
instructions.palette: Use very few colors with strong value hierarchy and preserve distinct identity markings as simple regions.
instructions.texture: Keep surfaces completely smooth and free from grain, hatching, or decorative detail.
instructions.rendering: Render a compact minimal character with generous facial spacing and the same shape vocabulary in every state.

negative_constraints: Do not remove identity-critical markings, props, or facial features to achieve minimalism.
Avoid vanishingly thin limbs, ambiguous merged body parts, and decorative background geometry.
No scenery, floor shadows, detached decorations, clipped extremities, or changing surface motifs between animation frames.
use_cases: Small icons, compact companion pets, and accessibility-oriented visual systems.
limitations: Minimalism cannot override explicit identity requirements; highly detailed references may need an adaptation warning.

compatibility.scaling: Keep the fixed target cell geometry; downsample the isolated artwork once with the recommended filter, preserve alpha, and inspect facial details at actual size.
notes: Use antialiased simple shapes with stable opaque fills; inspect negative gaps between limbs after scaling.
Keep texture landmarks and material highlights anchored to the approved character across all poses.

styles.name: Monochrome
styles.description: A value-only color treatment that preserves the approved construction while replacing hue differences with readable lightness steps.

instructions.materials: Use clean opaque flat illustration by default, or retain an explicitly requested underlying medium, and apply a single-hue tonal treatment.
instructions.forms: Preserve the approved silhouette and body proportions while separating adjacent parts through clear value regions.
instructions.linework: Keep the underlying contour system and strengthen facial lines only when required for value separation.
instructions.shading: Use a small stable ladder of lightness values to preserve volume, material cues, and readable markings.
instructions.palette: Choose one hue family or neutral grayscale with clearly spaced light, midtone, and dark values.
instructions.texture: Retain the original medium texture at restrained contrast so it does not compete with the face.
instructions.rendering: Render the same approved character in a controlled monochrome value system across all frames.

negative_constraints: Do not merge identity-critical markings that were previously separated only by color.
Avoid arbitrary hue changes, crushed black facial features, and pale silhouettes disappearing on white.
No scenery, floor shadows, detached decorations, clipped extremities, or changing surface motifs between animation frames.
use_cases: A restrained single-hue treatment for an existing character style.
limitations: This is a palette treatment and is not counted as a distinct base artistic technique.

compatibility.scaling: Keep the fixed target cell geometry; downsample the isolated artwork once with the recommended filter, preserve alpha, and inspect facial details at actual size.
notes: Preserve existing alpha and edge behavior; check the single hue against the chroma key and test both light and dark backgrounds.
Keep texture landmarks and material highlights anchored to the approved character across all poses.

styles.name: Duotone
styles.description: A two-ink color treatment with stable tonal mapping and clear separation of facial landmarks.

instructions.materials: Use clean flat printed illustration by default, or retain an explicitly requested medium, remapped to two opaque inks and controlled overlap tones.
instructions.forms: Keep approved character geometry and allocate distinct tonal regions to the face, limbs, and signature markings.
instructions.linework: Use the darker ink for essential contours and facial features while preserving the existing line rhythm.
instructions.shading: Map highlights and shadows through a stable two-ink tonal curve without unrelated gradients or extra accent colors.
instructions.palette: Choose two inks with sufficient value contrast and define how their overlap represents the darkest regions.
instructions.texture: Keep existing texture subordinate to the two-ink mapping and prevent fine grain from breaking facial shapes.
instructions.rendering: Render a consistent duotone treatment with identical ink roles and tonal mapping in every animation frame.

negative_constraints: Do not substitute arbitrary two-color recoloring that destroys marking or material distinctions.
Avoid a third accent color, unreadable midtone faces, and frame-dependent tonal remapping.
No scenery, floor shadows, detached decorations, clipped extremities, or changing surface motifs between animation frames.
use_cases: A two-color print-like treatment for existing mascot artwork.
limitations: This is a palette treatment and is not counted as a distinct base artistic technique.

compatibility.scaling: Keep the fixed target cell geometry; downsample the isolated artwork once with the recommended filter, preserve alpha, and inspect facial details at actual size.
notes: Retain source alpha; chroma must differ from both inks and their mixed tones, and opaque highlight regions must stay opaque.

styles.name: Pastel Flat

instructions.materials: Use clean flat cartoon illustration by default, or the approved flat construction, with opaque matte pastel regions and no glossy material effect.
instructions.forms: Preserve the approved compact shapes and keep adjoining body regions separated through outline or value contrast.
instructions.linework: Use a stable darker contour or facial ink tone to keep pale fills legible at small size.
instructions.shading: Use flat fills with at most one broad slightly darker region for anatomical overlap.
instructions.palette: Choose a limited pastel palette with enough value difference to preserve face, limbs, and identity markings.
instructions.texture: Keep surfaces smooth and untextured so the light-color treatment does not introduce noisy shading.
instructions.rendering: Render the same flat character with consistent pastel assignments and clear opacity on every background.

negative_constraints: Do not make pale regions translucent or remove contrasting facial features.
Avoid equally light neighboring colors that merge the silhouette and internal anatomy.
No scenery, floor shadows, detached decorations, clipped extremities, or changing surface motifs between animation frames.

styles.name: Neon Outline
styles.description: A graphic mascot defined by thick luminous-looking contour bands around a dark readable core.

instructions.materials: Use opaque digital color with bright neon-like contour bands and a stable dark interior body fill.
instructions.forms: Simplify anatomy into broad compact masses and short rounded line-supported limbs.
instructions.linework: Draw a thick bright outer contour and a few readable luminous facial marks with consistent line width.
instructions.shading: Use a restrained lighter center within each contour band to suggest emission without external glow.
instructions.palette: Choose one or two neon accent colors over a stable dark core and keep face colors clearly distinguished.
instructions.texture: Keep lines smooth and solid with no flickering noise, particle sparks, or uneven electrical filaments.
instructions.rendering: Render an isolated neon-outline mascot whose entire luminous effect stays inside its owned silhouette.

negative_constraints: Do not add neon signs, cables, text, or detached halos around the figure.
Avoid hair-thin lines, transparent body interiors, and glow that floods neighboring cells.
No scenery, floor shadows, detached decorations, clipped extremities, or changing surface motifs between animation frames.
use_cases: High-contrast digital companions and compact luminous graphic mascots.
limitations: Actual light emission is simulated with color bands; clean sprite edges take priority over atmospheric glow.

styles.name: Gradient Illustration

instructions.materials: Use opaque digital illustration shapes with smooth controlled gradient fills and no physical surface texture.
instructions.forms: Build rounded geometric body masses with distinct overlapping planes and an uncluttered facial area.
instructions.linework: Define forms primarily through color boundaries, adding only minimal opaque facial or separation lines.
instructions.shading: Use one broad directional gradient per major body shape with consistent light direction and restrained contrast.
instructions.palette: Choose coordinated gradient endpoints from the approved palette without introducing unrelated rainbow transitions.
instructions.texture: Keep fills smooth and band-free, with no grain, stippling, or noisy mesh patterns.
instructions.rendering: Render an isolated gradient-modeled character with the same endpoint colors and gradient orientation across all poses.

negative_constraints: Do not replace shape construction with a full-frame gradient background.

styles.name: Silhouette

instructions.forms: Encode identity in a compact unmistakable outer contour with separated limbs and a few broad intentional gaps.
instructions.linework: Use the silhouette boundary as the primary line; facial cues may be limited to a few robust negative-space cutouts.
instructions.shading: Keep the figure completely flat without interior tonal modeling, gradients, or cast shadows.
instructions.palette: Choose one solid high-contrast fill color and preserve any explicitly required identity colors only through an approved adaptation.
instructions.texture: Keep the interior smooth and uniform with no grain or decorative pattern.
instructions.rendering: Render clear contour-led poses with stable cutouts and enough separation to recognize each required action.

negative_constraints: Do not add a landscape, spotlight, projected shadow, or backlit scene.
Avoid merged limbs, tiny apertures, and silently dropping identity requirements dependent on color or markings.

instructions.texture: Keep surfaces smooth and pattern-free so internal cutouts remain the main visual feature.
